doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Collegians' half-board scholarship and other black college dance bands
summary: The Collegians were extracurricular with a half-board scholarship; Foster compares Tennessee State, Howard, Lincoln and Kentucky State bands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What was going on in terms of the school’s music program? I mean was the Collegians an official thing or -­

No, the Collegians was an extracurricular entity, but we did have a scholarship established in my first year there. This scholarship paid half our board for the school year. In other words, if the entire cost of eating came to $1,200 for the school year, $600 of that was paid by the scholarship. So we used to joke about it, a half-board scholarship. Wd we used to think of it as a half-ass scholarship [laughs].
Bands like this were typical of black schools though, weren’t they?
Yes, yes. Tennessee State Collegians --
I think Frank Wess played in a group called the Collegians at Howard.
The Howard Swing Masters.

The Swing Masters, right. Foster:: Then there was a Lincoln University. I don’t know what they called themselves. There’s one -- Kentucky State had one. I actually went on the road with them. I had a girlfriend from Covington, Kentucky, across the river from Cincinnati, who went to Kentucky State.
Which is located where? Where’s Kentucky -­

In Frankfurt, Kentucky. They had a band almost as good as ours, if not -­ maybe it might have been a little better. They traveled -- I went down to the campus to visit her, and they traveled as far as Lima, Ohio.
Which is up near Cleveland.
Yeah, right. It’s closer to Toledo. It’s in the northwestern section of Ohio.
That’s my hometown.
Toledo?
Yeah.
You don’t know about Lima?
Well I know about Lima. I know it’s up there somewhere.
Yeah, it’s up there somewhere.
I think from to Toledo, we went towards Cleveland to get to it, maybe that’s why I think of it, because if you go west from Toledo, you’re going to Detroit.
Yeah, you’re going to Detroit.
So you’ve got to go east.
You’ve got to go east, yeah, right, exactly.
So to me it’s like going -- I’m thinking I’m going to Cleveland.
Yeah, right. Lima is like southeast of Toledo. It’s got to be.
Okay, maybe, yeah.
And southwest of Cleveland [laughs].
Yeah, okay.
